newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann mulls future in MMBG.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann mulls future in MMBG.

text.p: German publisher Bertelsmann AG said on Monday it was considering its future involvement in the MMBG pay television consortium after Deutsche Telekom, the group's biggest shareholder, said it would pull out.
"We are also considering our position," a Bertelsmann spokesman said in response to a Reuter enquiry. A decision will not be taken before a meeting of MMBG shareholders this week.

Telekom, which has a 27 percent share in the pay TV group, confirmed newspaper reports on Monday that it would withdraw from MMBG. The Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said Telekom wanted to make its cable operation profitable by offering digital pay TV to its 5.5 million subscribers.
Other shareholders in the MMBG group are French pay TV group Canal Plus, German commercial TV broadcaster RTL and public broadcasters ARD and ZDF.
The move is a further blow to Bertelsmann's plans to play a dominant role in the new German pay TV market, in which Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch has gained a head start.
Bertelsmann has yet to launch digital TV programming, but remains, through its TV merger with Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion CLT, Europe's largest free TV broadcaster.
Consortium sources said that, following the announcement of Telekom's planned pullout, the MMBG group was "as good as dead".
